title: VPC Heal Policy Orchestration Syllabus
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Private VPC customers sometimes see transient and persistent node degradations (probe timeouts, drifted Terraform state, and long cold boot times) that require fast, safe remediation. Current runbooks are fragmented and many automated remediations either overstep (force-apply infra changes) or are too conservative (require manual triage).

Goal: Produce a single, policy-driven 'syllabus' that defines: (1) deterministic failure fingerprints, (2) prioritized non-destructive remediation actions, (3) gating and approval windows, and (4) terraform-aware repair flows that avoid state thrash. This ticket covers the orchestration spec, prototype automation rules, safety constraints, monitoring signals, and an operator-facing playbook for escalations.
acceptance_criteria: Documented failure fingerprints (probe timeouts, endpoint DNS flaps, KV cache miss storms, terraform drift counters) with metric thresholds and example alerts

A set of 3 canonical policy rules implemented in the heal-controller that perform only non-destructive remediation (reboot node, rotate instance in pool, resync Terraform state plan-dry-run) based on fingerprint matches
Automations include a staged gating: automated attempt -> wait window -> automated rollback option -> operator approval required for destructive actions
Integration tests that simulate 4 failure modes and assert the controller triggers the correct policy and records audit events
Runbook section published in Confluence and linked from the private console incident UI

decision_log: Prefer non-destructive actions first (drain, soft-restart, resync cache) to avoid causing customer-impacting state changes.
Terraform 'apply' is allowed only after an operator approval or an automated safety-check sequence: plan-diff is empty OR approved by 2-step automated verifier.
Use fingerprinting based on multi-signal correlation (probe failure rate + node boot latency + terraform-drift counter) to avoid single-metric flapping.
Controller emits full audit record and links to the Terraform plan output before any change; this will be surfaced in Console and in incident emails.
notes:
Trade-offs: More aggressive automated repairs reduce MTTD/MTTR but risk cascading changes when underlying infra provider is unstable. Chose conservative defaults and made them configurable per-customer.

Operational runbook excerpts included in Confluence link; will iterate based on SRE runbook drills in Feb cycle.
